source_excerpt: As of December 25, 2021, the Company expects 64% of total deferred revenue to be realized in less than a year, 27% within one-to-two years, 8% within two-to-three years and 1% in greater than three years.
decision_title: Segment Deferred Revenue Recognition by Contract Duration
trigger: Observed concentration of deferred revenue realization within 1‑year horizon prompting need for more granular forecasting.
decision_description: The Board will approve a new policy that classifies deferred revenue into short‑term (<1yr), medium‑term (1‑3yr), and long‑term (>3yr) buckets, each with distinct revenue recognition schedules to improve earnings guidance accuracy.
options_considered: Proceed:Adopt the segmented schedule immediately across all business units.;Pause:Maintain current aggregate recognition approach while gathering more data.;Revise:Implement a pilot for the short‑term bucket only, expanding later.
reasoning_summary: Segmentation aligns recognition with cash conversion patterns, reduces earnings volatility, and supports more precise guidance, outweighing implementation effort.
expected_profit_impact: Improved guidance may boost investor confidence, potentially increasing share price and lowering cost of capital.
profit_impact_pathway: More accurate revenue timing reduces earnings surprises, supporting higher market valuation and lower financing costs.
outcome_summary: If approved, revenue will be recognized in line with bucket schedules starting Q3 FY22, with expected reduction in earnings volatility.
conflicting_perspectives: Operations prefers a unified schedule to simplify systems, while Finance argues for granularity to improve guidance.

source_excerpt: In 2021, annual returns on the investment options available for the Deferred Compensation Plan generally ranged from -0.90% to 69.16%.
decision_title: Revise Investment Menu for Deferred Compensation Plan
trigger: Wide performance dispersion of plan investment options (-0.90% to 69.16%) highlighted risk‑return mismatch.
decision_description: The Compensation Committee will evaluate adding low‑volatility ESG‑aligned funds and removing underperforming options to better align with shareholder risk preferences and long‑term value creation.
options_considered: Proceed:Adopt the new fund lineup immediately across all participant accounts.;Pause:Maintain the existing menu until a full actuarial study is completed.;Revise:Implement a limited redesign that adds two ESG‑focused low‑volatility funds and retires the lowest‑performing option.
reasoning_summary: A partial revision balances risk mitigation with minimal disruption to existing participant allocations.
quantitative_signals: Current option range: -0.90% to 69.16%; target Sharpe improvement of 0.2; projected net cash flow impact $45M annually.
expected_profit_impact: Improved risk‑adjusted returns expected to increase net cash earnings by $45M per year.
profit_impact_pathway: Higher investment returns reduce the cost of deferred compensation liabilities, boosting operating income.
outcome_summary: If approved, new fund lineup to launch Q3 FY2022, with monitoring quarterly.
conflicting_perspectives: Some executives favor maintaining high‑growth options for upside, while risk officers advocate for more stable, ESG‑aligned funds.
master_agent_decision: Revise investment menu with a balanced mix of low‑volatility ESG funds and removal of underperforming options.
